extraction.name: Common Corpus
extraction.description: Common Corpus is a large open dataset for language model pre-training containing about two trillion tokens. It consists of uncopyrighted or permissively licensed data covering a wide variety of languages, domains, time periods, and code data.
extraction.creator: Pierre-Carl Langlais; Carlos Rosas Hinostroza; Mattia Nee; Catherine Amett; Pavel Chizhov; Eliot Krzystof Jones; Irène Girard; David Mach; Anastasia Stasenko; Ivan P. Yamshchikov
extraction.inLanguage: en, fr, de, es, la, it, pl, el, pt, ru
extraction.citeAs: Pierre-Carl Langlais, Carlos Rosas Hinostroza, Mattia Nee, Catherine Amett, Pavel Chizhov, Eliot Krzystof Jones, Irène Girard, David Mach, Anastasia Stasenko, Ivan P. Yamshchikov. Common Corpus: The Largest Collection of Ethical Data for LLM Pre-Training. arXiv:2506.01732v1, 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was assembled by aggregating existing open datasets, large dumps (Collections As Data), API retrievals (such as OpenAlex and Library of Congress APIs), web sources (Wikipedia, YouTube transcripts), and code repositories (The Stack), focusing exclusively on public domain and permissively licensed content.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis; Web API; User-generated content data
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The authors note a collection gap in the Open Science collection, mentioning that there are "some European-specific resources not currently well indexed on OpenAlex."
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include original PDF documents, raw XML output (METS/ALTO), mediawiki syntax dumps, RDF triples from Wikidata, audio transcripts from YouTube, SEC annual reports, digitized legal cases, and source code files.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Historical texts contain language that does not meet modern ethical standards, reflecting outdated cultural norms surrounding the discussion of certain ethnic groups, women, and themes such as violence.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Coverage for low-resource languages is still shallow; the amount of collected data is suitable for pre-training models of limited size but larger models will require significantly larger amounts of data; does not contain data for instruction-tuning and is not directly suitable for task-specific fine-tuning; curation methods do not have 100% accuracy; contains OCR errors that present considerable challenges to models.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Training models on historical texts could lead to the reproduction and circulation of harmful language, which the authors attempt to mitigate by removing or synthetically rewriting documents containing harmful language.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset originally contained Personally Identifiable Information (PII) such as phone numbers. The authors used Microsoft's Presidio to identify and replace PII with fictitious but realistic values.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Pre-training Large Language Models; developing open-data multimodal models and vision-language models (VLMs) for document segmentation and processing; developing language models with legal knowledge; training multilingual language models with diverse and creative writing styles; developing historical language models; training models on public domain code for coding applications or to improve natural language reasoning, world knowledge tasks, mathematics, and structured output tasks.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Common Corpus will remain an evolving resource reflecting the need for a continuous open infrastructure rather than a fixed dataset, with HuggingFace ensuring a proper archiving of past versions for reproducibility.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) was replaced with fictitious but realistic values. Documents containing harmful language were synthetically rewritten without the harmful language. On highly deteriorated content, the OCRonos tool was used as a synthetic rewriting tool.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Preprocessing included filtering files by language, file extension, and permissible licenses. Files consisting of 75% or more digits were removed, and sequences of [\r]+\n were replaced with \n. OCR errors, wrong word cuts or merges, and broken text structures were corrected using the OCRonos tool. Documents containing harmful language were removed, and PII was identified using Microsoft's Presidio.
